answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money, one active association worker and three inactive workers. 2. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4 face up. 3. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 4. Put side I of each of the five Action cards under a slot: Animals goes in slot 1 and the other four are randomly assigned among slots 2–5. 5. Randomly determine the starting player and play clockwise. Appeal starts staggered by turn order: first player at 0, second at 1, third at 2, fourth at 3.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Take 25 money”; “Draw 2 Final Scoring cards”; “Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4”; Animals under the leftmost slot; randomly determine a start player; appeal counter staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. In a two-player game, use six tokens of an unused color to block one level on each of the three face-up Base Conservation Project cards (left level of the left card, middle level of the middle card, right level of the right card) and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; these are unavailable to both players. 2. In a three-player game, three base projects are face up and no project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup. 3. In a four-player game, four base projects are face up and no project levels or donation spaces are blocked. 4. Reveal the six-card display after every player has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: four base projects in a four-player game, otherwise three; blocking applies only to two players; “After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.”

answers.answer: 1. After completing an action played from slot 4, move that card to slot 1 and shift the cards from slots 1–3 one slot right. 2. Set action strength before the action begins; each X-token spent then adds 1 strength, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. 3. X-tokens can raise action strength, including above 5 where allowed; a player may hold no more than 5. 4. An effect labeled “after finishing” resolves only after the action is complete, including moving the Action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: used card goes in slot 1 and intervening cards shift; “You set the strength before performing the action”; max five X-tokens; “‘After finishing’ effects” occur after card movement.

answers.answer: 1. No: a regular action may not be performed doing nothing; for example, a legal Animals action must play at least one animal, and Build must build a building. 2. If unable or unwilling to do a regular action, take exactly one X-token instead. 3. You still select an Action card, move it to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right; its strength and upgrade side do not matter. 4. You cannot take this alternative if you already have five X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “You may not do nothing”; X-token action takes exactly 1 token and still moves a selected Action card; unavailable at five held tokens.

answers.answer: 1. If the Break token reaches its last space during your turn, ignore extra movement beyond that space; the player who reaches it gains 1 X-token. 2. The current turn continues to completion, including any remaining action steps and effects. 3. The break occurs after that turn ends. 4. Following the break, return the Break token to its starting space for the player count and continue clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: “the break takes place after the end of your current turn,” reaching last space grants 1 X-token, and additional steps are ignored; break procedure resets token.

answers.answer: 1. On Cards I, advance the Break token 2 spaces, then either draw from the deck according to the strength table (maximum 3 drawn, with the indicated possible discard), or at strength 5+ snap exactly one display card of your choice. 2. On Cards II, also advance 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or reputation-range display in any order according to the upgraded table; strength 5 draws 4 and discards 1. Its snap option is available from strength 3 and takes exactly one display card. 3. The reputation-range restriction applies to Cards II's display-draw option, not snapping; snapping on either side allows any display folder. 4. Do not refill display cards taken during the action until the turn ends. 5. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the hand limit at breaks only.
answers.evidence: Cards action: Side I and II options, snap thresholds, and statement “On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation”; refill at end of turn; hand limit only at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. A display card is within reputation range when it is in the folder matching your Reputation counter or a lower-numbered folder; the folder-to-track mapping is 1→space 1, 2→spaces 2–3, 3→4–6, 4→7–9, 5→10–12, and 6→13–15. 2. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal per additional reputation step. 4. You may not inspect the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation spaces and rewards table and Reputation track: “Within reputation range” definition; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 convert each extra step to appeal; “You may not look through the discard pile.”

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly one building whose size is no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in that same action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a border space; each later building must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces within the map and do not cover water or rock; spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. A pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.
answers.evidence: Build action: side-I and side-II limits; placement rules; “Pay 2 money per space”; kiosk at least 3 spaces apart; each pavilion increases appeal by 1.

answers.answer: 1. Build I can build standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary (each size 5). 2. Each zoo may have at most one of each of the three special enclosure types. 3. The Build action cannot create unique buildings; those enter play only through Sponsor cards. 4. Once every map space except water and rock is covered, immediately gain 7 appeal; this can result from any effect that covers spaces, though Build II is needed for restricted-icon spaces.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table and Side II: “Unique buildings can never be built with this action”; full map condition grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Money, cards, and newly activated workers gained earlier in an action can be used for later steps in that same action. Resolve action items one at a time and pay for each item before receiving its own benefits; in particular, an animal's full cost must be paid before money gained from that animal is received. 2. Effects labeled “after finishing” wait until the entire action is complete, including Action-card movement. 3. Other effects resolve immediately; when multiple effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier bonuses may be used for later steps; pay each item before its benefits. Animal action distinguishes immediate versus “after finishing”; simultaneous effects' order is chosen by owner.

answers.answer: 1. Before playing each animal, meet every left-side condition, pay its printed cost, and provide legal housing; a matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the printed size; put one animal in it and flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side. 3. Petting Zoo animals can only use a Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, filling the indicated number of spaces with supply tokens; several animals may share if capacity permits. Petting Zoos have 3 spaces; the other special enclosures have 5 each. 4. Meet water/rock adjacency for whichever enclosure is chosen, counting distinct adjacent hexes, not edges. 5. Place the animal card and resolve its appeal, conservation, reputation and other effects. Ordinary effects happen immediately; “after finishing” effects wait until the whole Animals action, after the Animals card moves. When playing two animals, finish the first's steps before the second, but defer after-finishing effects.
answers.evidence: Animals action: numbered conditions, payment, housing and effects; enclosure-state table and special-enclosure capacity; terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits animal cards from the display if they are within your reputation range, in addition to hand cards; each display animal costs extra money equal to its folder number and the display is not replenished until turn end. 2. At strength 5 or more, you may gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before selecting/playing animals, so the increased range applies. 3. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals action, Side II: display animals within reputation range with folder-number additional cost; optional 1 reputation first at strength 5+; upgrade-conditioned animals permitted.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move corresponding eligible animals from standard enclosures into that newly built special enclosure; move all that fit and choose separately for each. The special enclosure must satisfy each moved animal's terrain adjacency and have sufficient free capacity. 2. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all of that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets size, flip none. 3. Mark the new special enclosure with the required number of supply player tokens per moved animal. This is relocation, not release.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure: “Only immediately” when built; choose each animal; fallback enclosure-flipping sequence; add tokens.

answers.answer: 1. The four Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2; gain a partner zoo 3; gain a university 4; conservation-project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task, requiring total action strength at least its task strength. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total task values do not exceed action strength. 3. Each task requires one active worker, but if one of your workers is already on that task you must place two workers instead; if three of your workers are already there, you cannot repeat it until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on that task have no effect.
answers.evidence: Association action: Side I one task and worker rules; listed task strengths; Side II one or more different tasks with total value limit.

answers.answer: 1. At setup, put one partner zoo of each continent and one university of each kind on the Association board; these are the available tiles players acquire. 2. On acquiring one, move it onto the lowest available space in that column of your map and take any covered-space bonus. A university also gives its printed reputation immediately. 3. You cannot acquire duplicate universities or partner zoos from a continent already represented in your zoo; partner zoos are limited to four total, and the third/fourth require Association II. 4. At breaks, restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and university kind, except kinds already owned by every player; do not add duplicates. 5. Universities provide their listed research/reputation benefits; only research icons count as zoo icons. The hand-limit university raises your hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not affect it. The limit is checked only at breaks.
answers.evidence: Setup 5a; Association task descriptions; break restocking; university table and restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. Association project work may support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II can instead take a project card from a display folder within reputation range, paying its folder number, without refilling until turn end. New projects enter the leftmost space above the Association board, shifting existing cards right. 2. To support, fulfill a printed condition and choose a reward level with no player's token on it; you normally may support a particular project only once, and never if it already has your token. Each reward level holds one token total across players. 3. Take one token from the left edge of your zoo map, place it on the chosen condition, then gain the depicted conservation and reputation. Uncovering the map token activates its bonus immediately, before or after project reward at your choice; recurring bonuses also recur at breaks. 4. Project-card capacity above the board is up to 2/3/4 cards for 2/3/4 players. If a new card exceeds capacity, discard the rightmost project and return tokens on it to owners' supplies; activated map bonuses remain activated. Tokens are not returned to maps.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work: sources, entrance, capacity/overflow, separate support limits, procedure and recurring bonuses.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. A release project's printed standard-enclosure category must match exactly: “2−” accepts printed size 1 or 2; “3” accepts size 3; “4+” accepts size 4 or 5. Actual tile size or special-enclosure capacity does not determine the category. 2. Before gaining conservation, lose only the animal's printed appeal and discard the animal card; its icons are lost. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and other earlier effects already earned. 3. If it could live in a special enclosure and its indicated special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone, or none if no enclosure meets size. 4. Playing a new release project grants 1 reputation; later supporting it does not grant that bonus.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects: exact printed-size categories, appeal/icon and retention rules, enclosure freeing fallback, and new-project reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand when action strength is at least its level and its conditions are met. 2. Sponsors II can play one or more cards from hand and/or reputation-range display; the sum of their levels must be no greater than action strength +1. Each display card also costs money equal to its folder number; refill display only at turn end. Sponsors II allows upgrade-required conditions. 3. Resolve cards sequentially, fully resolving each card's immediate effects before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action finishes. 4. If choosing the break-token money option, Sponsors I advances it by strength and takes that many money; Sponsors II advances it by strength and takes twice that much. The full money is received even if movement exceeds the remaining track spaces.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action side I and side II: level budget, sources, sequence and doubled money option; side-I full-money note.

answers.answer: 1. Break steps, in order: discard hand cards to limit; return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. The hand limit is normally 3 cards or 5 with the hand-limit university. 3. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion sharing at least one side with it; an empty standard enclosure does not qualify, but an empty special enclosure does. 4. Income order is appeal-based money, kiosk income, then Sponsor/map break income. If several players take display cards during break income, resolve those players clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), refilling the display after each such player's income before the next chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income definition; display-card income ordering and between-player refill.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose either an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or one Bonus tile beside that space; tile is executed immediately and removed, and the money option remains if tiles run out. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check the end at the end of a player's own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass each other. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of the affected player's own turn or a break. 3. If triggered at the end of a player's turn, that player finishes and every other player takes one final turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can yield at most 4 conservation points. Target Number is the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; victory points equal Appeal minus Target Number. Highest positive total wins; ties go to most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: conservation track rewards, exact trigger checks and final-turn rules, Final Scoring cap, VP calculation and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the nine Bonus tiles and place one randomly, face up, on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8. Do not cover the two yellow spaces with icons; return the other five tiles to the box. 2. When reaching 5 or 8 conservation, select one of the tiles beside that space or take 5 money; a selected tile resolves immediately and is removed. 3. Components are not a hard limit: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute, although explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Setup Bonus tiles; Conservation track rewards; Component supply: “use a suitable substitute.”

answers.answer: 1. For advanced maps, each player may take two random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and have players choose one each in reverse turn order. Return unselected maps to the box. 2. Map A is for first-time players; Map 0 is an intermediate option after a first game. 3. Map A begins with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk placed on its indicated spaces; the printed kiosk already counts as built and a kiosk tile is placed over it as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced map selection methods; Map A ability places an empty 3-space enclosure and kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. Put seven player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of each zoo map; keep the rest beside the map. 2. Hire inactive association workers from the lowest remaining reserve space upward. 3. Map A grants 2 conservation when its fourth partner zoo is gained, but its worker-related reward is a third partner zoo granting a worker; the general summary says certain zoo maps grant conservation when hiring the last worker. The specific reward for hiring the last worker depends on the map's printed bonus and is not enumerated for every map here.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place 7 player tokens” at map edge; “hire workers from the lowest supply space upward”; Map A bonuses list partner-zoo rewards; last-worker reward described as map-dependent.

answers.answer: 1. When you earn an Action-card upgrade, flip one chosen card from side I to side II without changing its slot. 2. Its improved action becomes usable from your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. An upgrade gained during an action does not change that action's strength or give it side-II capabilities. 4. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards because one of the four upgrade opportunities offers an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: stays in slot, improved action from next action, immediately counts for conditions; only four opportunities and one permits an alternative.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draws and discards at strength 1: 1 draw/1 discard; strength 2: 1/0; strength 3: 2/1; strength 4: 2/0; strength 5 or higher: 3/1. 2. If a discard is required, discard either one of the cards just drawn or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables, Side I row; “A required discard may be a newly drawn or previously held hand card.”

answers.answer: 1. Animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. 2. Bears count as a category even when also marked herbivore or predator. Petting Zoo animals are also their own category. Count both special categories unless the effect explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7) and Base glossary: shared principles list the seven and explain bears/Petting Zoo animals.

answers.answer: 1. Donation is available only with Association II, and each Association action may include at most one donation; you must perform at least one Association task in that same action. No worker is needed for the donation. 2. Pay the smallest still-visible donation cost and cover that space with a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space. Skip spaces blocked at setup. 3. Once all donation spaces except the last are covered, later donations each cost 12 money and place no further token.
answers.evidence: Association II donation: task prerequisite, costs, token placement and repeatable 12-money space.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards, plus partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or conservation-project icons. A university's reputation award and hand-limit mark are not zoo icons. 3. A card's own icons count for its effects, and doubled icons count twice; effects asking for different icon types count repeated copies as only one type. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules when they conflict.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo: included/excluded sources, own-card and doubled-icon rule; “Card text takes priority over general rules.”

answers.answer: 1. For a requirement for two water or rock spaces, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes. Two edges touching the same terrain hex count as only one; a larger continuous water/rock region counts only its individual hexes that are adjacent to the enclosure. 2. Terrain illustrations printed on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not satisfy requirements; connected regions do not make non-adjacent hexes count.
answers.evidence: Animals action: count distinct adjacent hexes; terrain adjacency clarification; illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. When you play a new Release into the Wild project, you gain 1 reputation; supporting an already-played release project does not grant that reputation. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same condition for all three reward spaces: choose any available level that is unoccupied under the usual support rules.
answers.evidence: Release projects: new card grants 1 reputation, later support does not. Icon-count projects: Breeding Program projects have same requirement for all three spaces; choose any available one.

answers.answer: 1. In “X : Y”, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2. If X has no number, the reward is paid once per fulfillment. 3. If X says “per,” the reward is paid per qualifying item. 4. If X uses numerical thresholds, a threshold reward is taken only once; when multiple thresholds are met, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: “X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward”; no number/per and numbered threshold rules.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply. 5. “Any zoo” includes those elements for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles gives the definitions of connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. A unique building must be placed while playing its Sponsor card; if it cannot legally fit, the Sponsor card cannot be played. 2. Use its matching tile, colored face up; rotate it freely but do not flip it. Follow ordinary placement rules and any printed water/rock adjacency requirement. No size-based construction payment is due. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and do not count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings: placement required with Sponsor; cannot play if impossible; tile/orientation/cost/placement and enclosure/terrain status.

answers.answer: 1. Finish the Animals action, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking a granted action. Then use the named Action card normally and move it to slot 1 after that action. 2. A named action, such as Sponsors, cannot be replaced with the X-token action. 3. Determination (Any Action) may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action/Determination timing, card movement and X-token alternative distinction.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion and Dominance search the unused face-down base-project deck: Assertion takes the chosen project; Dominance takes its named project. Return the deck afterward. 2. Dominance has no effect if its named project is already in play. 3. The acquired project goes to your hand; later play it and immediately support it through Association, placing it above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below it.
answers.evidence: Assertion / Dominance clarification: unused face-down deck source, no effect if named project already in play, later placement above board.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing the Animals action and moving the Animals card. 2. Clever puts its chosen Action card in slot 1; the cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5. Moving a card to slot 5 shifts the cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost / Clever clarification specifies timing, destinations and card shifts.

answers.answer: 1. An affected zoo must have at least 5 appeal for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering or Constriction. 2. Venom targets every other zoo with more appeal than yours that meets the 5-appeal floor. Hypnosis and Pilfering 1 target the highest-appeal eligible zoo, choosing among ties; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and most-conservation zoo, with each target meeting the floor. Constriction targets every other eligible zoo ahead on appeal and/or conservation. 3. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when determining affected players. 4. In multiplayer, players may replace interactive abilities with the alternative solo-marked text on those cards; this does not require playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities: eligibility floor, target reference table, animal appeal timing note, multiplayer alternative.

answers.answer: 1. Place Constriction tokens on each affected opponent's highest-slot Action cards: one token in slot 5 for Constriction 1, or two tokens in slots 4 and 5 for Constriction 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates to supply. 2. A marked card loses 2 strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action, and X-tokens can restore strength. 3. At effective strength zero or lower, you must spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card unused until it is at least slot 3. 4. Return the token after the affected action is used, or without effect during a break.
answers.evidence: Constriction clarification: highest slots, placement/count, no stacking, strength effect, response at zero or below and removal.

answers.answer: 1. A Constriction token reduces the card's strength by 2. If that leaves a card in slot 1 or 2 at effective strength zero or below, you cannot take its regular action at that strength; you may spend enough X-tokens to bring it to at least strength 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave it unused until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The alternative gives exactly 1 X-token, unless you already hold five, and still moves the selected card to slot 1.
answers.evidence: Constriction: card loses two strength; at effective strength zero or below, spend X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave until slot 3. X-token action is unavailable at five held tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 gives up to two selections; after each card, decide again which option to take: discard a display card, or discard a hand card and draw one from the deck. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replenished immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: choose up to twice between the options and decide after each; display discard is replaced immediately.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal may avoid using a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's printed standard-enclosure size. The same qualifying host herbivore can support any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 2. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot share that enclosure. 3. On release, the normal release/fallback procedure frees an occupied enclosure even if the flock animal originally shared it; you do not need to prove which animal historically occupied it.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification covers qualifying host, reuse, later non-flock animal and release without tracking historical residents.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to your notepad, where it is immediately usable. 2. If hiring that worker hires your last inactive worker, take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for that event. 3. If all workers are already active, Full-throated has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated: lowest reserve worker, map conservation reward for last worker, no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. Reveal the indicated number of deck cards; if none is an Animal card, discard all the revealed cards and add no card to your hand.
answers.evidence: Hunter X: “With no Animal among them, discard all.”

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis targets a zoo tied for highest appeal among eligible zoos; choose among ties. If your own zoo is the target, it has no effect. 2. You may copy only a target Action card in slot 1, 2 or 3. Use the target's upgraded or unupgraded side for the whole action, while other upgrade checks use your own cards; you may spend your own X-tokens. 3. Venom and Constriction tokens on the copied card affect you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally. 4. The summary does not separately state how a token on the copied card is oriented or which component area it goes to after removal beyond saying the Venom and Constriction tokens are discarded afterward.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification: tie/self rule, slots, side/upgrade rules, own X-tokens, copied-card tokens and card movement.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier on the Action card named by the reward; if the source is a Bonus tile, choose any Action card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, the card can execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength; move the card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution, so two tokens allow up to three actions. You may choose different permitted options for each execution. 4. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are complete. If a break is triggered in the first execution, it waits until the whole turn is finished. 5. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break. The summary does not say a break interrupts the second execution; it says the break waits until the whole turn is finished.
answers.evidence: Multiplier section: placement table and Two executions/X-tokens/additional multipliers/timing/return.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens on one Action card provide up to three executions of that action, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but you cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action. 3. The summary does not explicitly address taking X-tokens with a multiplied regular action except that each X-token boosts only one execution.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: additional tokens add one execution; “two tokens permit up to three actions”; may not mix X-token action with regular action; each X-token boosts only one execution.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking permits placing a Large Bird Aviary before Build is upgraded. You must not already have an Aviary and must have a legal site. 2. Other placement restrictions still apply, including the requirement for Build II to cover upgrade-restricted map spaces. 3. Posturing also follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time. 4. The summary does not give a separate alternative placement exception for Posturing beyond those normal rules.
answers.evidence: Peacocking and Posturing clarifications specify Build exception and normal placement/spacing and sequential placement.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animals give 3 appeal for the first, 6 for the second and 9 for the third. 2. A zoo may have at most three Petting Zoo animals because the single Petting Zoo has three spaces. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification gives 3/6/9 appeal, three-animal limit and small-animal status.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets the zoo with highest appeal among those with at least 5 appeal; choose among tied leaders. 2. Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo and the most-conservation zoo, each with at least 5 appeal; the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation. Choose among ties, and if the same zoo leads both tracks, pilfer from it twice. 3. If every player has zero conservation, Pilfering 2's conservation-target part has no effect, but its highest-appeal part still resolves subject to the normal floor. 4. If you select yourself as a target, that pilfering has no effect.
answers.evidence: Pilfering target reference and detailed Pilfering X clarification cover ties, zero conservation, double-targeting and self-target.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money. If they have less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve multiple pilferings one after another; the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: target chooses payment, card exclusions, missing-card/money fallbacks and sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch lets you tuck up to the stated number of hand cards beneath the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, but keep the appeal already gained. 2. Cards sold with Sunbathing go to the discard pile; you may sell up to X hand cards for 4 money each.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. A Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you choose one to discard when that milestone is reached. 2. At game end, score every Final Scoring card still remaining; each card is separately capped at 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification: extra card joins milestone discard choices; all remaining cards score, each with its own four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. For Scavenging, shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly from it, make the ability's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. For the illustrated Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1 and discard the other 2.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification specifies shuffle, random draw, stated selection and Scavenging 3 example.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet can take displayed Sponsor cards regardless of reputation range; if no Sponsor is present, it does nothing. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies to cards taken through these abilities.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification; general display rule says replenish at end of turn.

answers.answer: 1. Venom X places tokens on opponents' Action cards in the lowest slots, beginning at slot 1, with at most one token per card; return duplicates to supply. 2. When you use a card with a Venom token, remove that token and avoid all Venom fees for that turn; this also applies if you use it for the X-token alternative while holding fewer than five X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one Venom token remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money does not avoid the fee. 4. Unused Venom tokens are cleared at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X clarification gives placement, use, end-turn fee, inability-to-pay rule and break expiration.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian's immediate reward is 2 money for 1 university, 5 money for 2 universities, or 10 money for 3 universities. 2. While it is in your zoo, conservation-project work requires Association strength 4 rather than 5. 3. Its final-scoring reward is 1 conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 203 Veterinarian: I, R and F effects.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough's immediate reward is 2 appeal for each project previously supported, counted by player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map. 2. At each break it gives 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts the different continent and animal-category icon types in your zoo together, excluding research icons; count each type only once, even with duplicates or a double icon. Gain 1 conservation per two different types, rounding down. 2. Each other player gains 2 money for every conservation point you gain from this effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library immediately gives 1 appeal per research icon. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. At final scoring, it gives 1 conservation if its owner has five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas immediately gives 1 appeal per Americas icon. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, subject to normal placement and kiosk-spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia immediately gives 1 appeal per Australia icon. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program each receive two tokens from your supply when played. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one of these tokens to count as any one icon; never use both on the same support. 2. A base-origin project card later played above the board does not qualify; only projects still in the base row below qualify. 3. Their final-scoring condition is five or more project supports, counted by the tokens missing from the left edge of your map, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 215/218: two substitute tokens, base-row-only use, final scoring by supported-project count.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that same action, without increasing the action's strength requirement. Pay normal money and follow normal placement rules. 2. It permits only one extra building even if several different buildings are built, and the extra copy must be a building type not otherwise duplicated in the action; special enclosures still have a one-per-type zoo limit. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal for a full map except water and rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 217 Engineer: extra copy, payment/placement/limits and final reward.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher immediately gives 2 money per water or rock icon. 2. It allows you to cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered to qualify for a full map. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo. 4. Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers whenever you receive an actual placement bonus on a border space. For each such bonus, choose an additional uncovered placement bonus anywhere on your map; copied bonuses may be the same or different, and resolve them in your chosen order. 2. If multiple border placement bonuses are covered at once, each grants its own additional choice. The summary does not specify a special rule for simultaneous triggers beyond allowing several choices; identical bonuses may be selected. 3. Its final condition is that all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 221 Archaeologist: each actual border placement bonus allows one uncovered bonus choice; several triggers and final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording immediately grants 1 X-token. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but can place no more than one token on that project during a single Association action. 3. Each token placed counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab immediately gives 1 X-token. 2. Its owner is immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore that owner's counters and select the next qualifying player. 3. At final scoring it gives 1 conservation if the owner has all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. On playing WAZA Special Assignment, permanently choose small or large and mark the choice with a supply player token. Reveal cards from the deck until finding an animal of that size, keep it and discard the other revealed cards. 2. From then on, animals of the chosen size gain 2 extra appeal if small or 4 if large; you may not play animals of the opposite size. Size-3 animals remain legal but gain no bonus. 3. Size meanings: small is printed standard size 1 or 2, including Petting Zoo animals; large is 4 or 5.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 227 WAZA Special Assignment and size definitions.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program immediately gives 2 money per small animal. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals qualifies; it may play one extra small animal from hand with normal costs and rules, then take one small animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation. You may take the display animal even if you declined the extra play. 3. If the original Animals action mixes small and large animals, this effect does not apply. The display animal is taken as a card to hand; general display refill is at turn end.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 228 WAZA Small Animals Program; general display timing says cards taken from display are replenished at turn end.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist immediately gives 1 appeal per water icon. 2. Its recurring effect gives 1 money for each space newly covered that is adjacent to water, including multiple spaces in one building; a space touching multiple water hexes still pays only once. 3. Its final condition is that all water hexes are connected, meaning none is isolated, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building in the zoo, following applicable placement rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two cards from the deck, keeping one and discarding the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 249 Barred Owl Hut.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard any cards sold.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter, revealing a number of cards equal to your total predator icons; Hunter takes one revealed Animal card if available and discards the rest, or discards all if there is no Animal. 2. A new card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunter resolutions, with both newly played icons counted in each applicable total as the ability resolves.
answers.evidence: Spotted Hyena Compound: each predator icon uses Hunter based on total icons; a double-predator card triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time; Hunter clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters play with three supply tokens on its card. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a Sponsor card's level to play that Sponsor from your hand, meeting its normal conditions. 2. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when the Stable is played. It can be used at most three times, limited by its tokens. 3. The summary says the source is a hand Sponsor and the payment is its level; it does not state a separate display-card option.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School immediately gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation and must be placed covering at least two border spaces. 2. It also lets you take one display card within reputation range or draw one card from the deck. Resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is a unique building placed on two border spaces; it need not touch an existing building, but other placement rules apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break, it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. Because it is a unique building, adjacent kiosks count it for kiosk income. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal if the map is fully covered except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals immediately gives 1 appeal for each connected uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces never count. 2. At final scoring, count contiguous groups of empty building spaces separately and gain 1 conservation per six spaces, rounding down per group; e.g., groups of 13, 6, 3 and 2 give 2+1+0+0=3. 3. Upgrade-restricted empty spaces count even if Build is not upgraded. Terrain spaces do not count.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer immediately gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Its recurring effect gives 1 appeal and 2 money each time a new category or continent icon type is introduced into your zoo. 3. A newly played card with two copies of the same previously absent icon type grants the novelty reward only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program immediately permits a free size-5 standard enclosure, following ordinary placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, it lets you ignore one left-side condition, such as one required icon or the Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. This stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 263 WAZA Large Animal Program; Map 6 Research Institute clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your count of each animal-category icon with the player to your right and gives 1 conservation for each category where you have more icons. 2. If that player has no icons of a category, any one of your icons in that category is enough to have more. 3. The reward is capped at 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo 009.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 1, Observation Tower grants its bonus only to a standard enclosure adjacent to the tower hex itself; adjacency to a different rock hex is insufficient. Housing an animal in that enclosure gives the two appeal again even if an earlier animal was released. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 2, an enclosure qualifies when the standard enclosure touches the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. Such an enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; for example, physical size 2 counts as size 4. This cannot be ignored for release or relocation. 3. Outdoor Areas do not affect special enclosures and are not buildings.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Map 4 Commercial Harbor activates when a building is placed on its adjacent building space. Your first building may be placed beside the Harbor, but is not required to be. 2. Its discard ability can be used before, during or after your action, once per your own turn; never during a break or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Map 5 Park Restaurant gives break income of 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type or occupancy; each hex counts, including empty enclosures, and multiple hexes of the same building each count. 2. The Restaurant itself is not a building, so it does not count as a building for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus lets you place one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other ordinary placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 8, cover an H space by placing a building under ordinary placement rules. When covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor level is one lower. 4. The map's partner-zoo bonuses still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still need Build II to cover upgrade-restricted spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification.

answers.answer: 1. The pay-money-to-play-a-Sponsor bonus costs money equal to that Sponsor's level and requires its normal play conditions. 2. The card must come from your hand, even if Sponsors is upgraded; it cannot be taken from the display. 3. This bonus leaves the Sponsors Action card in its current slot; it does not move it.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: paid-Sponsor effect cost, condition, hand-only source and no Sponsors-card movement.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; any gains beyond those track ends are lost. 2. Reputation has a separate overflow rule: beyond 15, gain 1 appeal per remaining reputation step, provided you have the upgraded Cards action to progress to reputation 10+.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: appeal/conservation caps; Reputation track: at 15 further reputation converts to appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal, choose among ties; self-target has no effect, and only slots 1–3 may be copied. 3. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal and most-conservation eligible zoos, each with at least 5 appeal. Choose tied targets; a conservation leader needs at least 1 conservation, and if the same zoo leads both tracks it is targeted twice; self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction targets every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. A target ahead on one track receives one token in slot 5; one ahead on both receives two tokens, in slots 4 and 5.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference table and detailed Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from the animal's specified continent. A Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition allows a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-appeal condition permits play only while you have 25 or less appeal; its marker is a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. A bonus that ignores one condition removes one left-side requirement; it does not remove terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Animal versus Sponsor partner conditions; max-25 and minimum-reputation rules; ignore-one-condition definition.

answers.answer: 1. The illustrated Crested Porcupine Digging 2 offers up to two selections, choosing for each selection between (a) discard a display card and replenish it immediately, or (b) discard a hand card and draw one card from the deck. 2. After each selection, decide anew which option to use.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 (illustrated Crested Porcupine) clarification.

answers.answer: 1. At end of your turn after taking display cards, move cards from higher-numbered folders down to fill gaps, preserving their order, then fill remaining empty spaces from the deck. 2. During a break, discard cards from folders 1 and 2, move the remaining cards down, then refill the display. 3. During break income, if multiple players take display cards, refill after each player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Cards action: move cards down “keeping their order”; break procedure and display-income ordering/refill.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures with the empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. A placement bonus on a space covered by a building is gained immediately, once, when covered; placing an animal later and flipping the enclosure to occupied does not award that bonus again.
answers.evidence: Build action: standard enclosure empty-side-up; placement bonus granted immediately once; occupied flip does not repeat it.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, every player chooses one Final Scoring card to discard. Put it face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: all players discard a Final Scoring card “face down under the remaining pile.”

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; play proceeds clockwise. 2. The game has no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time until the end is triggered. 3. On an ordinary turn, perform one action using one of your five Action cards. Additional effects/bonuses may grant later actions, but they are not part of the ordinary single action.
answers.evidence: Setup: random start player and clockwise order; Overview: “does not play in formal rounds”; on a turn always perform one action.

answers.answer: 1. If nobody reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, every player must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: if no one reaches 10 before game ends, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
